chunks: 15. Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan and Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Imran al-Daqqaq (may Allah have mercy on them) both said: Ahmad ibn Yahya said: Bakr ibn Abd Allah ibn Hubayb said: Muhammad ibn Ubayd Allah told me: Ali ibn al-Hakam said: Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Aswad narrated from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father (peace be upon them), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) had two Jewish friends who believed in Musa, the Messenger of Allah. They came to Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and listened to him. They had read the Torah and the scriptures of Ibrahim and Musa (peace be upon them), and had knowledge of the earlier books. When Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, took His Messenger (peace be upon him and his family) [to death], they came asking about the one vested with authority after him, and said: 'Verily, a prophet does not die but he leaves behind a Caliph who executes affairs in his Ummah after him, who is close in kinship to him from his Household, of great significance and high prestige.' Then one of them asked his companion, 'Do you know the one vested with authority after this Prophet?' The other replied, 'I do not know him except by the description I find in the Torah: he is bald and pale, for he was the closest of the people to the Messenger of Allah.'

When they entered Medina and asked about the Caliph, they were guided to Abu Bakr. When they looked at him, they said: 'This is not our companion.' Then they asked him, 'What is your relationship with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family)?' He said, 'I am a man from his clan, and he was the husband of my daughter A'ishah.' They said, 'Is there any other [relationship]?' He said, 'No.' They said, 'This is not [the] kinship.' They said, 'Then inform us, where is your Lord?' He said, 'Above the seven heavens.' They said, 'Is there anything else?' He said, 'No.' They said, 'Guide us to one who is more learned than you, for you are not the man whose description we find in the Torah as the successor of this Prophet and his Caliph.' He became angry at their words and rose from them, then guided them to Umar, because he knew that if they confronted him with something, he would seize them.

When they came to him, they said, 'What is your relationship with this Prophet?' He said, 'I am from his clan, and he was the husband of my daughter Hafsa.' They said, 'Is there anything else?' He said, 'No.' They said, 'This is not kinship, nor is this the description we find in the Torah.' Then they asked him, 'Where is your Lord?' He said, 'Above the seven heavens.' They said, 'Is there anything else?' He said, 'No.' They said, 'Guide us to one who is more learned than you.' So he guided them to Ali, may the prayers of Allah be upon him.

When they came to him and looked at him, one of them said to his companion, 'Verily, he is the man whose description we find in the Torah: he is the successor of this Prophet, his Caliph, husband of his daughter, father of the two grandsons (al-Sabtayn), and the one who stands with the Truth after him.' Then they said to Ali (peace be upon him), 'O man, what is your relationship with the Messenger of Allah?' He said, 'He is my brother, I am his heir, his successor, and the first to believe in him, and I am the husband of his daughter Fatimah.' They said to him, 'This is the distinguished kinship and the close station, and this is the description we find in the Torah.'

Then they asked him, 'Where is your Lord, the Mighty and High?' Ali (peace and blessings be upon him) said to them, 'If you wish, I will inform you of what was during the time of your Prophet Musa (peace be upon him), and if you wish, I will inform you of what was during the time of our Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family).' They said, 'Inform us of what was during the time of our Prophet Musa (peace be upon him).'

Ali (peace be upon him) said: 'Four angels came: an angel from the East, an angel from the West, an angel from the Heaven, and an angel from the Earth. The one from the East asked the one from the West,

And as for what was during the time of our Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), that is His word in His Decisive Book: 'Nowhere is there a secret counsel between three persons but He is the fourth of them, nor (between) five but He is the sixth of them nor less than that nor more but He is with them where so ever they are.' [The Verse]

The two Jewish men said, 'Then what prevented your two companions from placing you in the position you deserve? We swear by the One who revealed the Torah to Musa: Verily, you are the true Caliph. We find your description in our books and read it in our synagogues. Verily, you are more worthy of this affair and more entitled to it than the one who has overpowered you with it.' Ali (peace be upon him) said, 'They preceded and obstructed [me], and their accounting is with Allah, the Mighty and High. They will be stopped and questioned.'

key_terms.أبو السبطين: Father of the two grandsons (Hasan and Husayn)
key_terms.صاحب الأمر: The one vested with authority / Caliph

ai.seo_question: Who were the two Jewish friends of the Prophet and how did they identify Ali as the true Caliph?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid* serves as a pivotal narrative for the Shia doctrine of *al-Ghaybah al-Sughra* (minor occultation) and the legitimacy of *Imamah*, utilizing the testimony of Jewish scholars to validate Ali’s succession through scriptural prophecy. The narrative contrasts the spatial limitations attributed to Abu Bakr and Umar with Ali’s citation of Surah Al-Mujadila 58:7, illustrating the Shia theological stance that God’s presence is not confined to a specific direction or place (*Makan*), thereby refuting anthropomorphic conceptions of the Divine. It underscores the concept of *Istidraj*, where the delay in Ali’s immediate appointment is viewed not as a denial of his right, but as a divine test for the companions.
